video_script.title: Same Flood, Same Vote, One Town Still in the Floodplain
video_script.hook:
August 1993: Two Mississippi River towns flood the same summer, hold the same relocation vote.

One town moved entirely.
body_slides: Aman watches from the cemetery hill. His town disappears below.
Thirty-five million dollars later. Every house moved to higher ground.
Two hundred miles north. Same flood, same vote. Almost nobody left.
video_script.voiceover_text: Thirty-five million dollars. Twenty-two agencies. An entire town rebuilt on higher ground after the 1993 floods. Two hundred miles away, same flood, same vote to relocate. Almost nobody left. Aman watches from the cemetery hill. His town disappears below. Thirty-five million dollars later. Every house moved to higher ground. Two hundred miles north. Same flood, same vote. Almost nobody left. Money doesn't move people. People move people. Follow for more stories like this at The Docket.

video_script.title: The Rate Changed. Phoenix Was Built for the Old One.
video_script.hook: New research suggests Phoenix's heat warning systems are based on outdated warming baselines while people die during what officials still classify as…
body_slides: Phoenix measures heat like it's still 1990.
The thermostats know what the maps don't.
Every moderate day kills more than the warnings.
video_script.voiceover_text: More than half of Phoenix heat deaths happened on moderate risk days last summer. Not extreme heat warnings. Just ordinary hot, day after day, in rooms where broken AC units sat silent. Phoenix measures heat like it's still 1990. The thermostats know what the maps don't. Every moderate day kills more than the warnings. The city was built for a climate that no longer exists. Follow for more stories like this at The Docket.
